title: Abu Hasan's Forgotten Mishap
summary: Abu Hasan was a wealthy and popular young merchant of Yemen who celebrated his lavish wedding feast surrounded by all the emirs, judges, and dignitaries of the city. The banquet...
full_text:
Abu Hasan was a wealthy and popular young merchant of Yemen who celebrated his lavish wedding feast surrounded by all the emirs, judges, and dignitaries of the city. The banquet was sumptuous, with roasted sheep, almond pastries, and fragrant sherbets flowing in abundance.

When the feast concluded and Abu Hasan arose to greet his guests at the threshold, he made an awkward, noisy slip upon the polished floor tiles, stumbling and tearing his fine silk trousers with a loud rip!

Paralyzed by agonizing embarrassment and imagining that the entire city would mock him forever, the sensitive youth did not even enter his bridal chamber. He slipped out through the garden gate, mounted his swiftest mare, and galloped into the desert!

He boarded a merchant vessel in the port, sailed to India, and settled in the distant city of Calicut. For ten long years he lived in exile, amassing a second fortune in the spice trade, yet tormented every single day by the bitter memory of his wedding night mishap.

At last, overwhelmed by homesickness, Abu Hasan returned to Yemen in disguise. As he approached his native village, he sat beside a well outside the walls to listen to the talk of the town.

An old woman was speaking to her young daughter: 'Daughter, when were you born?' The girl replied: 'I was born, mother, on the tenth day of the spring festival, the year of the great locust harvest.' The mother nodded: 'Ah yes, the year of the locusts, five years after the great flood.'

Abu Hasan listened closely, expecting to hear someone mention 'the year Abu Hasan ripped his trousers at his wedding.' He asked the elders at the coffee shop, the market vendors, and the guards at the gate: not a single soul remembered his blunder! Everyone remembered his generosity, his honest father, and his abandoned mansion.

Abu Hasan laughed aloud at his own foolish vanity: 'For ten years I lived in exile over a trifle that everyone forgot in ten days!' He returned to his home, embraced his family, and lived in honored joy, having learned that the world is far too busy with its own affairs to remember our minor embarrassments.
moral: Do not let social embarrassment drive you into exile; time washes away minor blunders, and life moves on.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "How Abu Hasan Brake Wind"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
